_comment: The hybrid pitch cut (scripts/build_pitch_video.py): real iPhone footage (inputs/, never committed) around the app recorded in the emulator. The beats are the take's, as in cinematic-2026.json (scripts/make-cinematic-video.mjs paces the take by these lines); 'hook', 'pinch' and 'poke' are the real clips with their in and out points (seconds); the carer's phone is the real companion page, captured at iPhone 13 size by scripts/capture_mobile_ui.ts; the hook's captions are her own words in English. Her request in the take is her own voice from the hook (mic), heard by the real Amazon Transcribe in Spanish (lang=es-ES); Nova answers in Spanish, in a Spanish voice; nova_captions maps each answer Nova gave (her exact Spanish) to its English; the edit lists any answer still without one. 'seed' is the take's workspace, ops dispatched before it starts (real tasks, not the first-run tutorial); the gaze beat's 'target' is the card the head rests on.
title: SpatialDesk
subtitle: A workspace that adapts to your body, in mixed reality.
disclosure: The interface is the real app, recorded in Meta's IWER emulator (Quest 3) and driven by a script, with live Amazon Nova and Amazon Transcribe. The hand gestures were filmed separately; the carer's phone is the real companion page, captured at iPhone 13 size.
_sfx_space: Where on screen each effect's panels are, read off the cut's frames: pan from -1 (left edge) to 1 (right edge), width from 0 (a point) to 1 (as made), over seconds. The glide's air starts wide at Apply's key as every panel comes in and closes on the agent's card; the landing is the Done column as the view reaches it; the tap is the phone's key.
metrics: frame time at the 95th percentile, CPU throttled 3x (Meta's IWSDK starter scene: 29.4 ms)
draw calls, under a budget of 80
the network drops: one calm line, and the cards still move by hand
end_line: A workspace that adapts to you.
_veil: Where her face is in each clip, so the edit can blur it (scripts/build_pitch_video.py's veil()): an oval's centre and radii as fractions of the frame, read off frames every half second, with a margin. The contest's rules allow no identifiable person other than the entrant; her hands, her sofa and her voice stay.

captions.text:
Hoy es un mal día, acércalo todo.
Today is a bad day. Bring everything closer.

beats.text: SpatialDesk fits the space to her body. First: where is she sitting?
On the sofa, everything comes lower and closer. She pinches wherever her hand is comfortable: that is her reach.
The space glides into reach, and settles with an amber glow.
She says what she needs, in her own words. Amazon Transcribe hears her, and while Amazon Nova thinks, an orb breathes.
Hoy es un mal día, acércalo todo.
beats.caption: Today is a bad day. Bring everything closer.

beats.text: Nothing changes until she agrees. She applies it, and every panel glides closer.
Her head turns to a card and rests there. After a second, a soft rim breathes around it: for Nova, that card is now this.
She says: move this to done.
beats.caption: Mueve esto a hecho. (Move this to done.)

beats.text: She pushes Apply with a fingertip. The key gives way under it, and the call to Rocío moves to Done.
Someone who cares can help, from a phone.
One large button, Help, recalibrate, opens the guided setup in her headset.
SpatialDesk: a workspace that adapts to you.

_extra: The second take (scripts/capture_extra_take.mjs), cut in after the setup reopens: the same real app in two of Meta's synthetic rooms (IWER's Synthetic Environment Module, shown as passthrough), Fit room in each, then one switch undoing the last change, then the network failing and a card moved by hand. Each beat waits for its line, like the first take. 'callouts' are the app's own words for an event of the take, shown large because on its panel they are too small to read (the network's notice comes from the take itself).

beats.text: In her real room, Fit room finds the desk and the walls: the board lands on the desk, and an anchor keeps it there tomorrow.
One switch is enough: the controls light up in turn, and one press undoes the last change.
When the network drops, she is told once, calmly, and her board still works by hand.
Another room, another desk: the same words, a different place.
